would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The RUNBOOK dead-worker-recovery section never gains the half-launched-task case — the attempt changes only the two scripts, so the operator-facing doc the launcher itself points at is left silent on the new failure mode.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order's DoD names the RUNBOOK update explicitly because the operator-facing surface changed, and both new refusal texts send the operator to "RUNBOOK, 'Dead worker recovery'" (hive-launch:146, hive-launch:278) for a case that section does not describe. An operator hitting a half-launch — task owned on the board, clones and wrapper issued, no pane — gets a stderr print that survives only as long as the terminal scrollback; the moment it is lost or the operator finds the stranded task later (board shows assigned, no window), the doc they are told to consult has no entry for recognising a half-launch, no statement that re-running hive-launch is wrong, and no manual finish procedure. That is exactly the archaeology the order set out to end.
